clue.text: Obtained tea using sneaky trick

blocks.note: past tense of get, meaning obtained
cha is an informal British word for tea

explanation.surface: Someone helps themselves to a cuppa by means of an underhand ruse.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA (also char) is old British slang for tea, from the Chinese word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gotcha is an informal noun for a catch or trap that springs on the unwary, a crafty ruse.

clue.text: Flat perhaps with no air left?

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat note is one example of being off pitch
second meaning, whimsical: an air is a melody, so having none left means lacking a melody

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' and 'no air left' both suggest a deflated tyre; the musical sense of air as a song is the key.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing or playing off the correct pitch, such as a semitone low, is described as being off-key.

clue.text: Tightly grip uncle’s French armchair in the middle

indicators.note: only the central part of each word is wanted, the core letters

blocks.note: the central letters of uncle
the central pair of French
the central pair of armchair

explanation.surface: Someone clutches hard at the centre of a relative's Gallic easy chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle has five letters, so its two middle letters are taken from either side of the true centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To clench is to close one's hand or teeth firmly round something, holding it hard.

clue.text: Result of following US subject

blocks.note: after means following on from
Americans call mathematics math, not maths

explanation.surface: An outcome of pursuing an American school course.
explanation.definitionFit: The aftermath is the consequences or period following an event, especially an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Ladies maybe into uncouth sort? It’s very revealing

indicators.note: going into something means sitting inside it, so the first item is placed within the second

blocks.note: a lout is a rough, ill-mannered person
a ladies is a women's public toilet, one example of a WC (water closet)

explanation.surface: A boorish man barges into the women's room, a scene that is exposing in more ways than one.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the Ladies' is the women's toilet; 'maybe' marks it as just one kind of WC.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-cut dress or top has a neckline cut deep, showing plenty of the wearer's chest.

clue.text: Begin looking into building really attractive sign

indicators.note: the beginnings of the following words are what is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Advice to start viewing a property that is a truly appealing building.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve zodiac signs used in astrology.

clue.text: Blubber when a few halt getting thrown out

indicators.note: being thrown out jumbles things up, so the letters land in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: People sob when a handful of stragglers are ejected from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' looks like the verb to weep noisily; here it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Blubber is the thick layer of fat under the skin of whales and seals, once boiled down for oil.

clue.text: Somewhat cute ritual places we’ve all been in originally

definitions.text: places we’ve all been in originally

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of, so a portion of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A charming ceremony held in the places where we all started out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful roundabout description rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Every person began life inside a mother's womb, and these are the plural of that organ.

clue.text: Obvious hiding place for one sick individual

indicators.note: something that hides a thing keeps it out of sight inside itself

blocks.note: patent can mean plain, evident to all
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An unsubtle spot to conceal an ill person, perhaps from the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: PATENT is read here as the adjective meaning plain or manifest, not the inventor's licence.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient is a person under medical care, typically someone ill being treated by a doctor.

clue.text: Characteristic strain suffered when buying a house

blocks.note: a property is a quality or attribute
to tax is to stretch or burden, a strain

explanation.surface: The typical stress endured by anyone going through a house purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain suffered' reads as stress felt; the definition actually starts at 'suffered'.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy charged on real estate is something a homebuyer must pay out, an unwelcome cost borne with the purchase.

clue.text: Strengthen couple in the lead

blocks.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
a team that is up is ahead

explanation.surface: A sports commentary note: the pair now ahead must reinforce their position.
explanation.definitionFit: To brace up is to fortify or steady something, making it firmer and better able to resist.

clue.text: Radar sees two of them

blocks.note: surface reading: a radar screen detects a pair of objects such as aircraft
setter's reading: the words radar and sees are each spelt the same forwards and backwards, so the clue contains two examples

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: 'them' points at a kind of word, and two such words open the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that read identically in either direction, like level or madam, belong to this category of wordplay.

clue.text: Bureau run by substantial type suited to command?

blocks.note: a bureau is an office or department
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
material can mean significant or relevant, as in a material fact

explanation.surface: An office managed by a weighty figure who seems born to lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substantial type' reads as a hefty person, but the definition takes 'type' with what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone described as officer material shows the leadership qualities needed for a commissioned rank in the armed forces.

clue.text: Consider cycling to find birds

indicators.note: cycling round moves the letters on, so the front letter goes to the back

blocks.note: to muse is to ponder or think over

explanation.surface: A suggestion to take up cycling as a way of spotting wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless Australian birds, related to the ostrich and cassowary.

clue.text: Mad family is an accident waiting to happen

blocks.note: bananas is slang for crazy
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A warning that a crazy household is bound to end in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the cartoon pratfall: anyone stepping on one is sure to slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana skin is a figurative term for a hidden pitfall likely to cause an embarrassing blunder, from the slapstick slip.

clue.text: Granules I melted to make carrier

indicators.note: melted things lose their shape and resettle, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Crystals dissolved together to produce something that holds or transports them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrier' suggests a container; in the trade it means an airline. Aer Lingus is Ireland's national airline.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is called a carrier because it carries passengers and freight; this one is the Irish flag carrier.

clue.text: Dismissed as soon as it started

blocks.note: first meaning: thrown out or sent off
second meaning: began, as a football match does

explanation.surface: A player sent off the moment the match got under way.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses come from football: being booted off the pitch and getting the game going.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both expelled from somewhere and commenced, as with a match beginning at the whistle.

clue.text: Belt tune out when high on this narcotic stuff?

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or askew, so the letters are put into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sings a song loudly while intoxicated on a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: To belt out a tune is to sing it loudly, so 'out' hides in a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the areca palm is chewed across South and Southeast Asia as a mild stimulant drug.

clue.text: Attending twice with some soothing words

blocks.note: someone attending is present, there
the same word again

explanation.surface: Someone shows up repeatedly to offer comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled phrase is what people say to calm a crying child or console someone upset.

clue.text: Wound from cleaning out septic abductor

indicators.note: cleaning something out empties its insides, so only the edges remain

blocks.note: first and last letters of septic
first and last letters of abductor

explanation.surface: Infection from a dirty kidnapper leaves a lasting mark, or a muscle injury after surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cleaning an infected abductor muscle; really both words lose their middles.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a noun, a wound is an injury, and a scar is the mark such an injury leaves; crosswords treat them as equivalent.

clue.text: Little support for home force arrival

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this piece comes below the others

blocks.note: being in means being at home
F is the physics symbol for force
low can mean small in amount

explanation.surface: A home team lacks backing as a strong newcomer turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflow is a coming in, as of money, people or water, so it is a kind of arrival.

clue.text: Hate one minister whipped up delivering such motivational guff?

indicators.note: whipping something up stirs it vigorously, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A loathed politician gets an audience fired up by spouting empty pep-talk slogans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipped up' suggests a crowd or whipping in Parliament; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a stock management cliché urging people to put the group before self, the sort of inspirational phrase many find hollow.

clue.text: Chap contributes some rising system measurements

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters sit inside the words that follow
in a down entry rising means going upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A man adds a few of his gauge readings for an upward-moving system.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just a man's name, as in the Irish patriot Robert Emmet; in Cornwall an emmet is also a tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet is a male first name, so a chap could bear it; crosswords often define names this loosely.

clue.text: Only half of Cannes gets cosy housing

indicators.note: half of each word is kept and the other half discarded

blocks.note: the back three of its six letters
the back two of its four letters

explanation.surface: A slice of the Riviera resort supplies snug accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds' nests are snug homes, and a nest is used figuratively for any comfortable dwelling.

clue.text: Complex mix seen as source of rigid compilers’ code

indicators.note: something complex is tangled, so the letters are knotted into a fresh order

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tangled blend viewed as the origin of a strict rulebook.
explanation.walkthrough: Ximenes was the pen name of Derrick Macnutt, Observer setter whose book set out the strict rules of fair clueing.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict, rule-following setters are called Ximenean because they follow the principles laid down by this famous compiler.

clue.text: Audacity works to build careers

blocks.note: gall is cheek or nerve
OPS is short for opera, the plural of opus

explanation.surface: Boldness pays off in advancing one's professional life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careers' looks like a plural noun about jobs; it is the verb meaning to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, career means to move swiftly and uncontrollably, much as a horse runs at full speed.

clue.text: Announces data about Europe

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one item wraps round the other

blocks.note: stats is short for statistics, numerical data
E abbreviates Europe or European

explanation.surface: Someone publishes figures concerning the European continent.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to declare or say it formally, so announces is a direct synonym in the present tense.

clue.text: Defeated and cut

blocks.note: first meaning: to see off a rival, beating them
second meaning: removed by sawing

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are past tense: saw is the past of see, as in saw off a challenger, and also the verb for cutting with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both seeing off an opponent and severing something with a toothed blade.
